fields.title: Days of the week

fields.title: Timezone
fields.help: An IANA name, for example Europe/London. Blank = UTC.

steps.hint: Runs at the times shown, in the timezone chosen. A time missed while the platform restarts still runs if it is less than 5 minutes late.

steps.label: Camera event

fields.text: Starts when a rule on this camera matches what a model finds, at most once in the rule's cooldown. Read the event as {{trigger.source.name}}, {{trigger.matched}} and {{trigger.frame_time}}. {{trigger.image}} is the frame, for a vision step. A step opens the frame with {{trigger.snapshot_url}} (it works for 15 minutes after the run starts); {{trigger.snapshot_link}} is for a signed-in person.

fields.title: Camera id
fields.placeholder: from the camera's page in Training Data

steps.hint: Publish the workflow to have it start. It starts only for a camera of this workflow's workspace.

trigger.description: the camera event (event, source {id, name}, rule, frame_time, matched, answer, image, snapshot_link, snapshot_url)

steps.label: Each camera frame
steps.sub: A stream answers each frame with this workflow

fields.text: Runs on every frame of a stream that uses this workflow. {{trigger.image}} is the frame (its privacy masks already applied), {{trigger.frame}} its number, {{trigger.t}} its time in the video (seconds) and {{trigger.source.name}} the camera. Only Find, Filter, Crop and Draw objects, Condition and For-each can follow it: the objects of the last Find or Filter step that ran are the frame's answer, which the camera's zones, lines and rules then read.

steps.hint: Publish the workflow, then choose it when you start a stream in Training Data (Cloud Streaming). Each Find objects call of each frame is paid from the balance of the person who started the stream.

trigger.description: the frame (image, frame, t, stream, source {id, name} or null)

<field>.description: each field of data.output_schema, when data.output_mode is json or schema

fields.placeholder: leave blank to use your default

steps.label: Find objects
steps.sub: Run a vision model on an image

fields.title: Image
fields.help: An image from an earlier step or from the trigger: a manual trigger's image input, a camera event's {{trigger.image}}, or {{nodes.<id>.output.image}}.

fields.title: Model
fields.help: A model of one of your Training Data projects (its test server or staging deployment must be running), or a ready model. Each image is paid from your balance at the model's price.

fields.title: What to find
fields.help: SAM 3 finds exactly these. For other models it keeps only these classes. Comma separated, for example person, car. Empty keeps every class.

steps.hint: A Test run does not call the model and charges nothing: it shows an empty answer. Use Run to find objects on a real image.

detections.description: what the model found, in the image's pixels

image.description: the image the model looked at

cost_usd.description: the provider's cost of the call (what the run's spend counts)

price_usd.description: what you were charged for the call (the platform markup included)

steps.hint: Read-only tools run unattended; approval-required tools are blocked in workflows.

steps.label: Run script

fields.title: Code (Python)
fields.placeholder:
from PIL import Image

img = Image.open('../input/image.jpg')
img.convert('L').save('../output/image.png')
print('done')
fields.help: Runs in a sandbox with no internet and no keys. What it prints is the step's text; an image it saves as ../output/image.png (or .jpg, .webp) is the step's image.

fields.title: Or a saved script (optional)
fields.help: A saved script of one of your agents, for code that needs the internet or a key. Use the code box or a saved script, not both.

fields.title: Image (optional)
fields.help: One image the script works on. It reads it as ../input/image.jpg (or .png, .webp); ../input/inputs.json names every file it was given.

fields.title: Images (optional)
fields.help: Several images, for example the crops of a Crop objects step, separated by commas. The script reads them as ../input/images/0.jpg, 1.jpg… At most 10 images, 20 MB in all, with Image.

fields.title: Detections (optional)
fields.help: What a Find objects (or Filter objects) step found. The script reads it as ../input/detections.json, every box in the pixels of its image.

steps.hint: Runs in a sandbox, never on AADML's servers. A script that writes ../output/image.jpg (or .png or .webp) gives the next steps that image as {{nodes.<id>.output.image}}. A Test run does not run the script. A stream's frames cannot run a script: each run of a script is a sandbox run, and a stream's frames run only steps without side effects.

stderr.description: what the script wrote to stderr

image.description: the image the script wrote to ../output/image.jpg, .png or .webp, when it wrote one

results.description: one {item, status, error, text, output} per item

fields.title: Seconds to wait
fields.help: Up to 60 seconds the step waits in place. A longer delay pauses the run and resumes it when the time is up.

steps.label: Data table
steps.sub: Store and read rows in a workspace table

fields.title: Operation
options: Get one row (by a unique column)

fields.title: Table
fields.help: A Data Table of this workflow's workspace (Workflows > Tables). The workflow reads and writes it as its owner.

fields.title: Values
fields.help: One value per column. A template is written as its value: {{nodes.find.output.count}} is the number.

fields.title: Rows (a list)
fields.help: A list from an earlier step. Each item is a row, or is read with the mapping below.

fields.title: Mapping (optional)
fields.help: Each column's value from the item, for example {{item.email}}. Empty: each item is written as it is.

fields.title: Unique column
fields.help: Get one finds the row whose unique column has the value; Upsert changes that row, or adds one.

fields.title: Filters
fields.help: Update and Delete need at least one filter.

fields.title: Limit (optional)
fields.help: Empty returns every matching row. With a limit, next_cursor reads the next page.

fields.title: Dry run (write nothing; say what would change)
On camera frames: only when something changed
fields.help: After Each camera frame, write a row only when its values differ from the last row this step wrote.

steps.hint: Update and Delete need a filter; Delete all rows asks on an approval card first. Exists has two outputs: exists and missing. A Test run reads for real and writes nothing. After Each camera frame only Insert can run: the rows are written together every 30 seconds or 500 rows.

row.description: insert, get_one, upsert: the row ({id, created_at, updated_at, <column>...})

rows.description: get_rows, update, delete (and insert_many with return_rows): the rows

count.description: how many rows were read, written, deleted or match

next_cursor.description: get_rows with a limit: the next page's cursor, empty on the last

exists.description: exists: whether a matching row exists (the exists / missing handles)

found.description: get_one: whether the row was found

created.description: upsert: whether a row was added

steps.label: Table row
steps.sub: A row was added or changed in a table

fields.text: Starts once for each row added or changed in the table, after the change is saved. Read the row as {{trigger.row.<column>}}, its id as {{trigger.row.id}} and what happened as {{trigger.change}} (added or changed).

fields.title: Table
fields.help: A Data Table of this workflow's workspace.

fields.title: Start when
options: A row is added or changed

steps.hint: A row this workflow writes itself never starts it again, and a chain of table workflows stops after 3.

trigger.description: the change (change, table {id, name}, row {id, created_at, updated_at, <column>...})

steps.label: SQL database

fields.title: Connection
fields.help: A database connection of this workspace (Settings > Connectors > Databases). The workflow uses it as its owner; a read-only connection can only read.

fields.title: Table
fields.help: Read from the connection. A name that is not in the database is refused.

fields.title: Columns (optional)
fields.help: Comma separated. Empty: every column.

fields.title: Filters
fields.help: Each value is sent as a bound parameter, never written into the SQL. Update and delete need at least one filter.

fields.title: Limit (optional)
fields.help: Empty returns every row (a large result is stored as an artifact, never cut). With a limit the output has next_cursor for the next page.

fields.title: Values
fields.help: Each value is a bound parameter. With a list of items, use {{item.<field>}}.

fields.title: Match on (unique columns)
fields.help: The column(s) of a unique key: a row with the same value is updated, else one is inserted.

fields.title: For each item (optional)
fields.help: A list: the values (and filters) are filled in once per item, from {{item}}.

fields.title: With a list of items
options: One transaction for all (rolled back on a failure)

fields.title: Query
fields.placeholder: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = $1 AND status = $2
fields.help: One statement. Put each value in the parameters below as $1, $2 … — {{ }} in the query is refused.

steps.hint: Reads never change the database; a read-only connection is enforced by the database itself. Each call has 60 seconds. A Test run does not connect to the database. After Each camera frame only Insert can run: the rows are written together, in one transaction, every 30 seconds or 500 rows.

rows.description: the rows read (select, query) or returned by the write

count.description: how many rows are in rows

affected.description: how many rows the write changed

next_cursor.description: the next page's cursor, when a limit was given and more may follow

steps.label: MongoDB

fields.title: Connection
fields.help: A database connection of this workspace (Settings > Connectors > Databases). The workflow uses it as its owner; a read-only connection can only read.

fields.title: Filter (JSON)
fields.help: A template only as a value, in quotes: it is inserted as data and can never become an operator. $where, $function and $accumulator are refused. A delete needs a filter.

fields.title: Pipeline (a JSON list of stages)
fields.help: $out and $merge are refused on a read-only connection.

steps.hint: A read-only connection can only find, count and aggregate. Each read has 60 seconds (maxTimeMS).

document.description: the document found (find one), or null

found.description: find one: whether a document matched

inserted_id.description: insert one: the new document's id

inserted_ids.description: insert many: the new documents' ids

steps.label: Redis
steps.sub: Get, set, keys, hashes, lists, publish

fields.title: Connection
fields.help: A database connection of this workspace (Settings > Connectors > Databases). The workflow uses it as its owner; a read-only connection can only read.

fields.title: Pattern
fields.help: Every matching key is returned (SCAN, never KEYS).

steps.hint: Only these operations: no raw command can be sent. A read-only connection can only read.

value.description: the value read, popped or incremented

receivers.description: publish: how many subscribers got it

steps.label: New database rows
steps.sub: New rows in a table or collection

fields.title: Connection
fields.help: A Postgres, MySQL, SQL Server or MongoDB connection of this workspace.

fields.title: Column that only grows
fields.help: An increasing id or an "updated at" time. A row whose value is larger than the last one seen is new.

fields.title: Start
options: One run per check, with all new rows

fields.title: Also run for the rows already there
fields.help: Off: the first check starts from now, so the rows already in the table are not run.

steps.hint: Publish the workflow to start checking. A paused workflow keeps its place and does not check; on resume it continues from there, so no row is missed or run twice. An empty check costs nothing.

trigger.description: one run per row: {row, cursor}; one run per check: {rows, count}
